title: SQS vs Pub/Sub: Which Scales Better? ⚡
fb_caption:
Amazon SQS vs Google Cloud Pub/Sub: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

- Throughput: SQS offers high throughput but can face FIFO limitations. Pub/Sub excels with massive, global scale and high message rates.
- Latency: Pub/Sub generally offers lower end-to-end latency for global distribution. SQS latency is typically low within a region.
- Consistency: SQS Standard offers at-least-once delivery, FIFO offers exactly-once. Pub/Sub guarantees at-least-once delivery.
- Failure Modes: SQS is highly available within a region. Pub/Sub is globally replicated, offering superior availability and disaster recovery.
- Operational Overhead: SQS requires more manual configuration for scaling and partitioning. Pub/Sub is largely managed and auto-scales.

Recommendation: For global, massive-scale, event-driven systems, Google Cloud Pub/Sub is often the superior choice due to its inherent scalability and global resilience. SQS is a strong contender for regional, less complex, or strictly ordered message processing.
